rationales.1: The count line and closure notice fit the first mobile viewport, but the oversized status-banner cards make the mobile page the longest of the set, so reaching specific trails takes substantial scrolling.
rationales.2: Each status combines color, icon, and text label with a legend, and the encoding stays identical from the header counts to every card.
rationales.3: No-report cards are explicit, the snowpack shows a dashed estimated badge with the sensor explanation, the chart marks July 22 as a no-data gap, and each card carries its report time.
rationales.4: Open, caution, closed, no report ordering with counts matches the decision flow in plain language, though the legend duplicating the section labels directly below it is redundant.
rationales.5: Spacing and card construction are consistent, but the full-width shouting banners repeating the same status word are drama rather than information priority, and the palette is stock traffic-light generic.
rationales.6: The cards absorb the data in both modes, but two-card sections leave a conspicuous empty third column on desktop and the banner repetition amplifies the closed cluster awkwardly.
rationales.7: There is no one-sentence signature beyond a generic traffic-light status dashboard, which reads as a transplanted pattern rather than something true of this service.
rationales.8: Mechanics are fully conventional with no breaks attempted, which stays inside the budget but spends none of it on distinction.
rationales.9: Microcopy such as no report received from this trail is competent but wholly generic, and any competitor could publish this page unchanged.
rationales.10: The header counts serve a quick glance and nothing is mandatory-playful, but the long banner-heavy scroll is mild friction for a daily habitual check.
